The district includes several specially designated areas — Gunnison Gorge National Conservation Area and Wilderness ; Canyons of the Ancients National Monument (along with its associated Visitor Center and Museum ); the Powderhorn Wilderness Area ; and the southern portion of Dominguez-Escalante National Conservation Area , including the Dominguez Canyons Wilderness. The Spring Creek Basin Wild Horse Herd Management Area is located within the Disappointment Valley in Tres Rios Field Office. The district encompasses approximately 7.26 million acres of subsurface minerals, including the natural gas wells of the Northern San Juan and Paradox basins and coal leases in the valley of the North Fork of the Gunnison River. Space Exploration and The Universe To build a complete picture of our universe, scientists gather information both in space and on Earth. Many of NASA’s tools that explore deep space rely on radioisotope power systems supported by the Department of Energy (DOE). DOE researchers also contribute to experiments conducted in space. On Earth, researchers use tools like supercomputers, particle detectors, and observatories to answer a variety of questions about our universe, including how the universe evolved, why it is expanding ever faster, and why there is matter at all. DOE’s Contribution to Understanding Our Universe The DOE and its predecessors have long supported NASA missions to space. DOE maintains the infrastructure to develop, manufacture, test, analyze, and deliver radioisotope power systems for space exploration and national security missions. These systems can produce heat and electricity under the harsh conditions in deep space for decades. NASA has used them for missions to study the moon and all of the planets in the solar system except for Mercury. pages.text: SpaceX Starship megarocket blasts off before expected return for reuse | SpaceX | The Guardian Skip to main content Skip to navigation SpaceX's Starship Flight 15 launches from Starbase in Boca Chica, Texas, on Friday. Photograph: Ricardo Arduengo/AFP/Getty Images View image in fullscreen SpaceX's Starship Flight 15 launches from Starbase in Boca Chica, Texas, on Friday. Photograph: Ricardo Arduengo/AFP/Getty Images SpaceX SpaceX Starship megarocket blasts off before expected return for reuse Flight 15 expected to orbit Earth about 14 times over 22 hours, before company catches it at Starbase, Texas Uwa Ede-Osifo Fri 13 Nov 2026 19.53 EST First published on Fri 13 Nov 2026 18.38 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google SpaceX’s Starship megarocket blasted off from Texas on Friday afternoon as the aerospace company sought to make history with a double catch of its reusable rocket, but ultimately fell short. Starship, the world’s largest rocket, standing at 407ft, is expected to orbit Earth about 14 times over the course of 22 hours, before the company catches the rocket at its launchpad at Starbase in south Texas . The rocket, which is on its 15th flight, is composed of two elements: the lower booster, with 33 Raptor engines that fired off during takeoff, and the Starship at the top. As smoke plumes wafted from the launch site, SpaceX employees erupted into cheers. SpaceX had planned for both components to return to its tower, but the booster, named Super Heavy, was aborted, and splashed down in the Gulf of Mexico. pages.description: Although booster exploded, company caught upper stage for first time in campaign to make megarocket reusable
pages.text: SpaceX’s Starship returns to launch pad from orbit in victory for company | SpaceX | The Guardian Skip to main content Skip to navigation 1:17 SpaceX’s Starship returns to launch pad from orbit – video SpaceX SpaceX’s Starship returns to launch pad from orbit in victory for company Although booster exploded, company caught upper stage for first time in campaign to make megarocket reusable Uwa Ede-Osifo Sat 14 Nov 2026 17.35 EST Last modified on Tue 17 Nov 2026 12.40 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google SpaceX ’s megarocket Starship returned to its Texas launch tower on Saturday, a milestone in the company’s efforts to make the craft suitable for human spaceflight. The 171ft (52-meter) bullet-shaped upper stage descended into the clutch of the tower’s mechanical arms, ending a 22-hour mission where the craft orbited Earth 14 times. Starship’s 15th test flight was envisioned as a historic double-catch mission, where all parts of the rocket would be returned intact to the launch site, rather than recovered from the ocean as with some previous test flights. The hulking spacecraft is comprised of two parts: a lower booster stage called Super Heavy, whose Raptor engines powered the orbital ascent, and an upper stage also called Starship. Those double-catch ambitions were dashed on Friday, when the booster diverted a few minutes after takeoff and exploded in the Gulf of Mexico. pages.title: Spain 2-3 England: How did Thomas Tuchel's side win and what was learned from Argentina defeat? - BBC Sport
pages.description: Trying to protect a lead in the closing stages, England have been here before - so how did they cling on against Spain?
pages.text: Spain 2-3 England: How did Thomas Tuchel's side win and what was learned from Argentina defeat? - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, James Trafford (right) kept Spain out in the latter stages By Emlyn Begley BBC Sport journalist Published 16 November 2026 England held on to beat Spain 3-2 with a backs-to-the-wall finale in the Nations League to finish top of their group. But many observers would have been feeling a sense of deja vu from the World Cup semi-final when England sat back and were beaten by Argentina . So what was different this time? BBC Sport has a look. Were the situations the same? First of all the context of the two games was entirely different. England were 1-0 up against Argentina in the 55th minute on neutral territory in Atlanta - and still had all their players. Anthony Gordon had put them ahead but Lionel Messi set up Enzo Fernandez and then Lautaro Martinez late on. But against Spain the best performance of Thomas Tuchel's reign had them 3-0 up through goals from Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White. Elliot Anderson then fouled Lamine Yamal for a penalty, which Mikel Oyarzabal scored - and that began the siege at a partisan Riyadh Air Metropolitano. Nico Williams made it 3-2 but Spain could not find an equaliser, thanks in part to England keeper James Trafford. "Half an hour feels like two hours against a team like this [with 10 men]," Tuchel told ITV afterwards. "That's the way it is. pages.description: England's stunning win in Spain had everything - and was their best under Thomas Tuchel, writes Phil McNulty.
pages.text: Spain 2-3 England: Three Lions produce best win under Thomas Tuchel - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Harry Kane scored for a record-equalling seventh England away game By Phil McNulty Chief football writer in Madrid Published 15 November 2026 Thomas Tuchel went with bold words when reminded about the caution that sabotaged England's World Cup hopes and left them with so much to prove against Spain in the Nations League on Sunday. In a media theatre at the Metropolitano in Madrid, head coach Tuchel's sixth sense led him to go public with what he was convinced England would produce against the world champions. Tuchel looked his inquisitors in the eyes and declared: "We are up for something spectacular." To say Tuchel and England kept their word was a masterpiece of understatement after the finest night of the head coach's reign resulted in a 3-2 victory that was large parts magnificent, some parts madness - and all parts spectacular. It also ended Spain's 43-game unbeaten run - setting aside their penalty shootout defeat by Portugal in the 2025 Nations League final. If England and Tuchel could be accused of being cowed by pressure when they led Argentina in the ill-fated World Cup semi-final, they were thrillingly positive in this unforgiving Madrid environment. The question being asked when England held a one-goal advantage through Harry Kane's penalty at half-time was 'what would theirs and Tuchel's reaction be?' Stick or twist? pages.description: As Spain prepare to host England in the Nations League, BBC Sport columnist Guillem Balague charts the rise of Unai Simon to become the world's best keeper.
pages.text: Spain v England: How Unai Simon became world's best goalkeeper - BBC Sport By Guillem Balague BBC Sport columnist Published 15 November 2026 Peter Schmeichel handed Unai Simon the Yashin Trophy and the room applauded warmly. Then the world's best goalkeeper spent his time talking about everybody else. Simon thanked his parents and his brother. He thanked his girlfriend for being an "oasis of tranquillity", and the friends from home who remind him that "many of us in this room are privileged". 'La cuadrilla', the gang of lifelong friends that is a traditional part of Basque culture, has a WhatsApp group of its own, and he takes them on holiday every summer. He thanked his coaches and team-mates. Like Simon, none of them are regulars on the covers of the media. Then he talked about a man who could not be in the room at last month's Ballon d'Or ceremony in London, but whose influence lives on - Simon's youth academy mentor Koldo Asua, who died in 2021. The Spain and Athletic Club number one is not your archetypal superstar. In fact, he is the complete opposite. He stays away from the headlines and is relatively low profile when compared with some of the game's other goalkeepers. His position as Spain's number is regularly questioned - as was the decision to name him as the world's best. In the part-beauty pageant election that is the Ballon d'Or, being low key can work against you, but the case on the pitch is easy to state - even though it rattles those who see the Premier League as the highest standard reachable. pages.description: Prosecutors begin investigating EU funds meant for upgrading the Spanish railway line where a train crash killed 69 people.
pages.text: Spain's rail authorities face European fraud probe after Urda rail disaster Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Spain's rail authorities face European fraud probe after Urda rail disaster 6 November 2026 Share Save Add as preferred on Google Alba Morgade EPA Last month's train crash in which 69 people died was the second deadly accident on the same high-speed line this year European Union prosecutors have begun investigating the possible misuse of EU funds meant for upgrading the Spanish railway line where a train crash killed 69 people last week. Prosecutors backed by a special unit of Spain's Guardia Civil security force said they were conducting the inquiry at the offices of Adif rail infrastructure authority and rail safety agency AESF. The 28 October accident on the Madrid-Seville high-speed line was one of the worst railway disasters in Europe this century. It is the second EU fraud inquiry opened into Spain's railways this year, after 46 people were killed on the same line at Adamuz in January. Last week, a train operated by state-owned operator Renfe ploughed into the back of a stationary train belonging to private Spanish company Iryo outside the village of Urda, around 130km (80 miles) south of Madrid. The LZB communication system that monitors the position of trains had gone down, and the Renfe train had been given the all clear to start running at normal speed, even though the Iryo train ahead of it had been unable to restart. The country was expressing its support of the Cuban and Filipino struggle against Spanish rule and responding to the mysterious explosion of the USS Maine in Havana Harbor in February 1898, which killed more than 250 American sailors. While the Spanish–American War was fought entirely overseas, national parks tell stories of training camps and military regiments. Some of the threats apparently came from phone calls, others via email, and although they have all turned out to be hoaxes, they were each clearly serious enough to force emergency action. Some planes had to be escorted by military jets, others were quietly inspected mid-air by cabin crew - desperate not to cause alarm. A number had to be re-routed from their original destinations, landing at different airports, sometimes in different countries. An Aer Lingus flight had to land at an airbase 1,000 kilometers from its intended destination after running low on fuel. On this page: Related Information Overview Eligibility Data Products Cost Estimate Expectations More Information Contact Us Overview A special census is a basic enumeration of population, housing units, group quarters and transitory locations that the U.S. Census Bureau conducts at the request of a governmental unit. If local officials believe their community’s population size or demographic composition changed considerably after the 2020 Census, a special census can update population estimates produced by the Census Bureau. However, it cannot review or recount 2020 Census results. Local officials can request a full special census for their community or jurisdiction or a partial special census. A partial special census is conducted using the same methodologies and procedures as a regular or full special census. With a partial special census, however, the area being counted is typically much smaller. For example, governmental units may choose to conduct a partial special census with just those areas that might have experienced a large population growth or a boundary change. Please note that the governmental unit requesting the special census assumes full responsibility for the cost of the count. SRPs may be required for a range of activities – such as recreation services, organized events, competitive uses, and other related proposals – when necessary to manage visitor use, protect resources, ensure public health and safety, or support coordinated recreation management. SRPs help the BLM provide consistent access to recreation opportunities while sustaining public lands for current and future users. Spectrum sharing optimizes the use of the airwaves, or wireless communications channels, by enabling multiple categories of users to safely share the same frequency bands. Spectrum sharing is necessary because growing demand is crowding the airwaves . Smartphones and appliances, military and public safety radios, wearable devices, smart vehicles and countless other devices all depend on the same wireless bands of the electromagnetic spectrum to share data, voice and images. What is NIST’s Role? As the nation’s measurement authority, the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) develops measurement tools, data and methods to make fair, efficient spectrum sharing possible. This work supports not only the trillion-dollar U.S. telecommunications industry and its hundreds of millions of customers but also the U.S. military, which has spectrum in the 3.5-gigahertz (GHz) frequency band that is a focus of pioneering U.S. spectrum-sharing efforts . There are several ways to reach the Sahara, depending upon the bank balance, boldness, and backbone of the traveler. You can fly from Algiers and within a few hours be riding a camel through the palmeries of El Goléa or sitting atop the high dunes of In Salah. pages.text: Spiders may lure male fireflies to their death with a call of love | National Geographic ANIMALS Spiders may lure male fireflies to their death with a call of love A new study suggests orb-weaving spiders may manipulate the flashes of male fireflies caught in their web to mimic the mating call of a female. A male firefly is caught in the web of an orb-weaving spider, Araneus ventricosus . Researchers believe that these spiders may manipulate the bioluminescent signals that fireflies use to find mates. Photograph by Xinhua Fu By Gennaro Tomma Published August 19, 2024 Spiders have evolved an impressive array of hunting techniques—from trapping their prey with spit to building webs strong enough to capture snakes. Now, researchers have discovered a particularly malicious tactic that some orb-weaver spiders might use to trick fireflies into their webs. A new study published in Current Biology found that some spiders seem to manipulate the flashing signals of male fireflies they’ve ensnared in their webs to mimic the signals of a female. This glittering call of love attracts other male fireflies to the spider’s web, just like a siren song attracts sailors to death. ( These spiders lure their prey in very crafty ways .) The idea that spiders would put off a meal to use their prey as bait is in itself intriguing, says Dinesh Rao, a researcher at the Universidad Veracruzana who reviewed the paper but wasn’t involved in the study. “Spiders are always hungry, right? A better measurement of the neutron lifetime would give physicists greater clarity about the way our universe works. SPR Origins Origins The need for a national oil storage reserve has been recognized for at least five decades. Secretary of the Interior Harold Ickes advocated the stockpiling of emergency crude oil in 1944. President Truman's Minerals Policy Commission proposed a strategic oil supply in 1952. President Eisenhower suggested an oil reserve after the 1956 Suez Crisis. The Cabinet Task Force on Oil Import Control recommended a similar reserve in 1970. But few events so dramatically underscored the need for a strategic oil reserve as the 1973-74 oil embargo. The cutoff of oil flowing into the United States from the Arab members of the Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC), in response to American aid to Israel during the Yom Kippur War, sent economic shockwaves throughout the Nation. In the aftermath of the oil crises, the United States established the SPR. President Ford set the SPR into motion when he signed the Energy Policy and Conservation Act (EPCA) on December 22, 1975. The legislation declared it to be U.S. policy to establish a reserve of up to one billion barrels of petroleum. The Gulf of Mexico was a logical choice for oil storage sites. SPR Sales and Exchanges SPR Sales and Exchanges Sales Section 161 of the Energy Policy and Conservation Act (EPCA) gives authority to the President under specified conditions to direct the Secretary of Energy to conduct a public sale of oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve. DOE sells SPR oil in a competitive auction to the highest bidder. SPR Storage Sites Storage Sites Emergency crude oil is stored at the Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) in underground salt caverns at four major oil storage facilities in the Gulf Coast region of the United States, two sites in Texas (Bryan Mound and Big Hill), and two sites in Louisiana (West Hackberry and Bayou Choctaw). Created deep within the massive salt deposits that underlie most of the Texas and Louisiana coastline, the caverns offer the best security and are the most affordable means of storage, costing up to 10 times less than above ground tanks and 20 times less than hard rock mines. Strategic Petroleum Reserve caverns range in size from 6 to 37 million barrels in capacity; a typical cavern holds 10 million barrels and is cylindrical in shape with a diameter of 200 feet and a height of 2,500 feet. One storage cavern is large enough for Chicago's Willis Tower to fit inside with room to spare. The Reserve contains 60 of these huge underground caverns. These four sites have a combined authorized storage capacity of 714 million barrels. Storage locations along the Gulf Coast were selected because they provide the most flexible means for connecting to the Nation's commercial oil transport network. In NIST’s early years, railroad trains were derailing in epic proportions. In the first decade of the 20th century, the U.S. government recorded approximately 4,000 derailments a year, with an average of about 13,000 people killed or injured annually. One major cause was the fracturing of wheels. In 1905 the American Foundry Society approached the young agency with a solution: It had identified an alloy that would resist fracture. However, there was a still a problem: The foundries that would make the wheels lacked good sample materials that they could use as a reference in creating the alloys and maintaining quality control.
